dialogue.text: Gee, I thought my vision was perfect. And here I was, worshiping false eyeballs.
Very well. Shall I show you to your room, or would you prefer to be dragged off, kicking and screaming?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Ooh, kicking and screaming, please.
Then the calls began.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: ...Well, I... I think I may be coveting my own wife...
Oh. Oh. Matthew, 19:19, yeah, right, right. Well, you know, Ned. The Good Book says a gentle answer turneth away wrath.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: A gentle answer. Well, that is a jim-dandy idea. Bless you, Reverend.
Back off, Popey LaPew!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Bart and Homer can't go Catholic! The Romans have been separate from us since the Schism of Lourdes in 1573. And that was about our holy right to come to church with wet hair. Which we've since abolished.
Oh, uh, uh, ooh... bad dog. Look at that. Right on Ned's lawn. Now how could you do such a thing? Good boy, don't stop now. Bad dog! I condemn you to hell!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Better get the ol' snow shovel back from Homer, huh?
What the... oh, I get it.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Boys, I just talked to God. He's vacuuming Heaven to get it ready for when dead people show up. And He'd like you both to render a sacrifice.
Well... Aren't you being a tad melodramatic, Ned? Also, I believe Job was right-handed.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: But Reverend, I need to know. Is God punishing me?
You know you just pushed it up to list price! You know that, right?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Edna, I'm not one for costumes, but I sure do like that feather in your hair.
In the beginning...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Excuse me, Reverend? It's, ah, hard to hear you with those fans goin'.
HOMER SIMPSON'S BREATH IS STRONG / OH, THE DOO-DA --

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, hey, now hold on there. The nice people want to hear the real words.
Ugh, probably stepped on a worm. Hello, Ned.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, there's Homer Simpson! Oh, what a perfect opportunity to follow up on my letter.
Come on, boy. This is the spot -- right here. That's a good boy. Good boy. Do your dirty, sinful business.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Howdy, Reverend Lovejoy. Nice to see you there... on my lawn... with your dog.
... Judgment Day is upon us. I warned you the Lord wouldn't stand for your mini-dresses, and Beatle boots...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I resisted these for thirty-five years! Why did I wear them today?
That might seem to be true...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I sense a "but" coming, Reverend...

This so-called "new religion" is nothing but a pack of weird rituals and chants designed to take away the money of fools... Let us say the Lord's Prayer forty times. But first, let's pass the collection plate.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Looks like slim pickin's today, Reverend.
Jesus cried again with a loud voice, and yielded up his spirit.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Lord, forgive me for my pride. All-wise, as always, you have rightly raised Homer above me.
Good boy. Don't stop the music.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Marge Simpson -- still making juice the old-fashioned way?
Well, you know kids and vegetables. What was it, asparagus?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: No Reverend, the point is, he said a bad word.
Is that really devils food?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: No, it's angels food with chocolate on top.
Puh-leeze.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Now, Marge, don't you worry. We've all had our brushes with the law.
But I think you're up to the challenge, Ned.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh Reverend, I've been workin' my bible to the bone tryin' to save that man.
But Ned, I was singing the real words.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, let's just take it from the top.
HOMER'S BREATH SMELLS BAD!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, those are not the words!
Hello, Ned...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Reverend... Emergency... I... You... Simpson kids... Eedily... Baptism... Oodily... Doodily-doodily...
If this is about that stupid quarter again -- Hello, Ned.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Sorry to bother you, Reverend Lovejoy, but I'm kind of in a tizzy. Our son Todd just told us he didn't want to eat his "damn vegetables.
That's beautiful. We appreciate the kisses. Now, let us bow our heads in a silent prayer of thanksgiving.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Stop it! Breathe through your damn mouth!
And now, I have some exciting news. Tomorrow we'll be blessed with a visit from the highest ranking clergyman of our Presby-Lutheran faith, His Holiness... the Parson.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: The Parson?! He's coming here?
The service has ended. Go in Peace.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: The door's frozen shut... and it's the only way out!
And the winner is Ned Flanders!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: This is my favorite kind of surprise: mild!
Now if everyone would open your prayer books...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well boys, good thing we brought the eye soap.
Oh, oh right, yeah. Kids usually pick these things up from someplace. Find out who's doing it and... uh, direct them to the Bible.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Where in the Bible?
Marge, it's as plain as the bruise on my shin -- there's no place for me here.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Where you going, Reverend? The town's that way. Reverend? You're goin' the wrong way!
Hello, church basement.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yeah, it's Ned Flanders. The teens have been chasing me all night. They finally stopped to gas up their scooters.
Marge, we can't tell you how sorry we are.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You have our deepest condol-diddly-olences. I'm sorry. I'm just nervous, I didn't mean any disrespect.
So many little plastic Christmases ruined.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You want me to deliver the Christmas sermon? I feel like I'm born again again!
Are you the Beer Baron?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, if you're talking about root beer, I plead guilt-didilly-ilty as char-dardilly-arged.
I'm making Catholic Saint Stew!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: No -- not surf and Murph!
Our new primary directive becomes removing all impediments to the plant.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Uh, Homer, I'm afraid this is the part of God's perfect plan where you're murdered by robots.
Daddy, can we move closer?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Abso-not-ly, hot Roddy. We're up here, out of range of the crashes and the drivers' cussing.
I can't eat because my conscience is heavy.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Boys, enough of your shenanigans. It's bedtime.
Okay, "do-over mommy.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Boys, you will please call your new mother whatever she feels comfortable with.
But Mommy wanted it.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: But where do you put something that big?
Yeah, chillax, Daddy.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Chillax?! Young man, in the Flanders house, we speak the King's Diddily.
Daddy! Look how high I am!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: He chipped a tooth! How will he bite Wheat Thins? How?
I pick my Dad. Do you want to play capture the flag, Daddy?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Heh. Sports on a Sunday? Hm. I'd better check with Reverend--
But we forgive her.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hiya Marge. Rod and Todd in the land of nod?
We don't have to play football do we, Daddy?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Ho-ho-ho, you betcha. Team sports'll keep you away from temptations like rock music and girls.
Dad! Todd's speaking in tongues!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I wish he were, Rod, I pray for the day, but I'm afraid he's just delirious from fever.
Daddy, what are you doing?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Imploring people I never met to pressure a government with better things to do to punish a man who meant no harm for something nobody even saw. That's what I'm doing!
Daddy, did you make that devil's music?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: It wasn't me, boys! It was the train!
Daddy, can I buy this one?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Let's see... "Get Bent." Well, the only thing that could mean is kneel down and pray. We'll take the whole box. Get bent, everyone!
Look, Daddy. Todd is stupid and I'm with him. And now Mommy's stupid.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Lookin' good, Rod. Lookin' good.
Does Mr. Simpson have a demon, Daddy?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Looks like it. Run get Daddy's exorcism tongs.
Daddy, are you sure it's okay for us to watch cartoons?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Mmm-hmm. This one's fine and dandy, Roddy. It's approved by a council of Presbylutheran ministers.
I know!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: No, Son, we've got to let Bart and Lisa get one. C'mon, this one's easy.
So shall my knife find favor with thy belly!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Now I must bury my son, while you wander the earth forever, with the mark of evil upon your face.
But I have a girlfriend!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Now you've got a pen pal.
With his funny friend David.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, I'd put rocks into your pockets and walk you out to sea before that happened.
Can Mr. Simpson watch us every day?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, Roddy, he's not runnin' a day care center.
Daddy, something attacked me!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, now Roddy, it's just a stuck ball. I'll get it.
How come everybody's having visions, Daddy?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, there's no explaining God's will, Roddy. That's like explaining how an airplane flies.
I'm jealous of girls 'cause they get to wear dresses.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: One problem at a time, boy.
Run, Daddy, run!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Open the door, Maude! I don't have time for the secret knock!
Look, Daddy, I'm king of the mountain!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Rod, get off of there!
I'm already doing it!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Roddy, get down! You're gonna fall!
Yay!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Say, Todd, I want to talk to your Uncle Homer. You're head of the car till I get back.
When's Todd's solo, Dad?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Shhh. It's coming up, son, it's coming up.
I wish we could see their happy faces.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Sin of pride, Roddy.
Yay!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: So you see Mr. Roberts, I really would like my house back.
Daddy, where do babies come from?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Sweetie, that's not the kind of dress you wear outdoors... or indoors... or in a dirty dream.
Who brings baby storks?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: There's no such thing as storks! It's all God!
Daddy, what's the red stuff coming out of Kitty's ears?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Uh, er, that's just raspberry jam.
I think it says "Dell.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: We'll let the authorities sort that out.
Oh boy! Gramma!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: We're not going anywhere.
Daddy, all the fumes are making me dizzy.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well now Roddy, the Lord wouldn't let us die this way.
The secular humanist did it in the schoolhouse with misinformation!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, I think it's about time you boys get to bed.
I have a headache.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, sir, everyone's alive. Guess that's something to be thankful for.
Daddy, what are we gonna do today?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, we're gonna do what every kid your age likes to do: look at bread.
But it's in the "stay away" closet!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You just fetch it!
Did they make babies with their Mother? Or with each other?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Your mouth is hopin' for a soapin', boy! Now stop asking silly questions and go kill your brother!
I can't stand to be touched! Never tell anyone!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: And I haven't. Not until now.
Okay, now you are the worst.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: ... Rod says "Marco," and darn it if Todd doesn't say "Polo" right back! Oh, listen to me just running my gums about my kids. You're probably bored silly.
Well, then I'm staying in Springfield with you. For good.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Forgive my language, but I am one happy camper!
Ned, I love you, but I'm not ready to be tied down.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I love you, too. And I always will. But unlike the Bible, I guess this isn't gonna have a happy ending.
What does that one say, Ned?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: It says a man should make restitution if he eats his neighbor's grain. And that's good enough for me.
Ned, I know this is fast, but, when I go back to Hollywood I want you to come with me.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Ned Flanders in Tinseltown?
Ned, I've never met a man like you. You're sensitive, you're in great shape, you have a mustache, and yet you're not gay.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: No way! I won't even eat vegetables over two inches long.
Ned, I'm not sure you should open the door.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh now, if someone took the time to press that little button, this is the least I can do.
Fine, I'll wear your stupid jacket.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Sara, I love ya, but I get the feeling you're just... not a Ned-head tonight. Is something wrong?
Actually, there is something. The time we've spent together has been wonderful, but... I want sex. With you.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Se... well, that's a mighty big... kettle of... premarital... uh, doodly...
Wow. Wow. That made me completely forget about Bob Balaban.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: That's what Maude used to say.
I knew you'd say that. I need a glass of wine.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: This is quite a dil-diddly-lemma. I better talk this over with the big man.
You want to get married?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Uh hmm. That's right. I'm like Baskin Robbins. You get one free taste then you gotta buy the scoop.
Oh, loosen up Honey. This dress just creates the illusion of nudity.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, Siegfried and Roy create a lot of illusions, but I doubt their girlfriends dress like that.
A girl could get used to that.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, and you will. Right after the wedding.
You're so sweet to look out for me. The public may not see me naked, but you just might.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, that's uh, very interesting...
Where do you think I learned to do this?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa. This movie's turning into Sponge Bob No-Pants!
You know, I grew up in a house like this. I didn't know there were people like you left in the world.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yep, we occupy that useless mass of land between Los Angeles and New York. Called America!
Ned, we won!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yep. Now all we gotta do is turn that woman into a fella and that kiss into a game of Scrabble.
Hey keep it down, will ya? The part where all my men get killed is comin' up.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Listen Sheriff, I can help you take down Bonnie and Clyde.
Even I'm offended by this, and I'm a fat Southern sheriff.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Um... the battery seems to be dead. I'll get some help by hidin' in that bush.
Oh right, I gave myself gills.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I told you, the only dancing I like is "square.
That was an "inside me" bone!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Make way for Captain Coolerhead!
Never!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Marge, you know I thought I was Springfield's wing ding king, but uh, you make my chicken look like cock-a-diddily doo doo.
This place is the height of tedium.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, Maude, I turned your dream of a Christian amusement park into a bemusement park.
Those monsters must be stopped!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Perhaps I can be of some assistance.
Why does every church meeting end this way?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: We want you to teach alternative theories to Darwinian evolution.
How are those two comely boarders of yours, Ned?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, Mel, they're swell.
EVERYONE WHO COUNTS LOVES NED FLANDERS.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Knock that off, you two. It's time for church!
HENS LOVE ROOSTERS / GEESE LOVE GANDERS / EVERYONE ELSE LOVES NED FLANDERS...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: MY MOUSTACHE / IS BRISTLY / MY LETTERS / ARE EPISTLY / AND I DON'T WANNA / MISLEAD YOU / I LIKE TO HUG AND KISSLY--
If you ever get into trouble, all you need to do is...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Feels like I'm wearin' nothin' at all. Nothin' at all, nothin' at all...
She'd say that year off from Princeton was the worst decision I ever made.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well son, if you take responsibility for your actions, this could be the start of a better life for you.
Golly, Sergeant Carter, I can't fix your jeep. But maybe this will make it up to you. Galveston, oh Galveston...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Is this all he watches?
Ned, they gave me the game ball. I want you to have it.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Stan, tell you what -- Homer Simpson here is just about the biggest Atom fan that's ever graced God's green earth. I bet he'd enjoy it, even more than me.
To live "among them" is to die!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: This could go late -- we haven't even ordered pizzas and pop yet. Can you handle Rod and Todd's parent-teacher conference for me?
O" IS FOR OH BOY, WE LOVE OUR LEADER / "N" IS FOR THE BEST KOREA, NORTH / "G" IS FOR GEE WHIZ, WE LOVE OUR LEADER

dialogue.text: We just wanted to give you all a big thank you from Team Nedna.
Good evening. I'm Edward Christian, Assistant VP of Finance and Distribution at PolyStar Pictures.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Dang! I should've brought the camera.
I'm afraid you'll have to lose the uh... hippie lip.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Get rid of Dr. Fuzzenstein? Why, I couldn't dream of thinking about considering...
Sure. What would you like -- four years? Five years?

dialogue.speaker: NED
dialogue.text: So, Simpson. You're really moving to Capital City?
Yeah! Nine yards!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Okilly-dokilly, let's put on our game faces.
From the looks of that moustache, I'm guessing you're a tenured professor at the people's republic of Berkeley.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, the only thing left-wing about me is the way I write.
That's all right, she can munch on an antler. Antlers ain't meat.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I thought I smelled death-a-diddly. What is that, an eight-pointer?
Hey, where have been all my life?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Thank you, Plow King-a-lee-ding.
Nuclear secrets... pictures of Lenny... everything I need for my plan!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Marge, that dinner was a winner! What's for dessert?
You're right, that was harsh. Tell you what, maybe I could donate the park, as a tax write-off.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: If you could do that, I'd make this place a shining beacon for the Lord.
Christian, eh? Wellll, that's different.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Now the thing is, I don't have a lot of money...
Oh, you are so full of it! God's grace, that is. It's really sickening...there aren't more people like you. Now get out...your pen and we'll make it official.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, bless you, sir.
Sell Storytime Village?! Why, you gotta be off your tuffet!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, it's been closed for so long... and-and I thought I could turn it into a Christian theme park.
I know. T'oodley doodley.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Ah, kids can be a trial sometimes.
I said I don't want any damn vegetables.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: All right, that's it, young man. No Bible stories for you tonight.
Yes, Daddy.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: And so we don't have another disaster, you crawl up those steps!
Daddy, get up. You'll be late for church.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Eh, you boys can go with the Simpsons. I'm not going to church today.
Help meeeeee... eeeeeee... eeeee.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Flanders to God, Flanders to God! Get off your cloud and save my Todd.
Glass of water on the side for dippin'.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Gosh darn it! Am I that pre-diddley-dictable? I've wasted my whole dang diddley life.
We shall come rejoicing, bringing in the Sheaves.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: He's not getting it from his brother, that's for darn sure.
Dad, the heathen's getting away.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I see him, son.
Dad, can I anoint the sores on his feet?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I think it's Mom's turn, son.
I knew he would.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I'll be right back, boys. I'm going to go help that lady.
Hey!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: It says "Show me your tie." It's cute. C'mon, let's go.
What train, Daddy?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: It was right there... with the... and the...
RISE AND SHINE AND GIVE GOD YOUR GLORY, GLORY...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Me and the boys made you breakfast in bed. It's the best darn diddly way to start your first Flanders day!
Daddy, where's Mommy? We miss her.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Mommy had to go away. She's with God, now.
Hey, Dad, thanks for helping me with my science project.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: My pleasure, Study Buddy.
Daddy, was Mommy a monkey? I can't remember!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: No one was ever a monkey! Everything is what it was and always will be! God put us here and that's that!
Dad, should I poke Rod with a sharp thing like the mouse did?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: No, son. No sirree, Bob.
You sure buried him deep, Daddy.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Not so deep the Lord can't find him... and judge him.
There's one little boy you should watch out for. He's a bad, bad little boy.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Now, Todd, don't scare the president.
Aw.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Now, boys, Mr. Simpson is the guest. He gets to decide what to watch.
Off the rim!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh! Almost. Boy that was close.
I don't like this story.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, imagine that -- sleeping quietly after a bug attack! Oh, and Todd's as dry as a bone! Lisa, you're a wonder! I'm going to recommend you to everybody!
I've got the best Dad in the whole world.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, you know how that embarrasses me.
Let's build it for her, Daddy.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Ohhh, that's a nice thought, Toddy, but to build an amusement park you need lots of money, and manpower, and turnstiles...
Daddy, what do taxes pay for?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Ohhh, why, everything! Policemen, trees, sunshine. And let's not forget the folks who just don't feel like workin', God bless 'em.
Let every evil lung fill!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Okay, I've got two of every animal. But only males -- I don't want any hanky-panky. Hey, hey, hey, cut that out!
Yayyy!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Sara, I'm sorry, but I can't move to Hollywood. Heck, even Dollywood's too far out for me. Too many people appreciating it ironically.
Daddy, I'm scared!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: But the infinite beauty-- / But the Bible says--
Can't talk now, Flanders. I've got a class to teach.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: But you rang my...
Fine, I'll never go back. Starting tomorrow. Today is Lenny's birthday and they're having ice cream cake.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: But you're gonna kill us all...
The father of the boy who doesn't win has to mow the lawn in his wife's Sunday dress.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: But... neither, I mean we're both... I mean, you have to do it too.
We do that every night! Come on! Jump on the bed!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Can I help you, stranger?
... I FEEL LIKE MAKIN' LOVE / MAKIN' LOVE TO YOU! / DO DO DOOO / DO DO DOOO.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Catchy song, all right. You really wrote it?
Look at 'em, with their bright, airy narthex and light, flaky Eucharist. I wouldn't mind dipping my hand in their font.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Christ is born, who's on my horn?
Flanders? What are you doing here?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Christmas is my busy season. Sold three pairs of scissors this month! Two came back.
Son, I'd love to, but... I'm a deacon now. My butt's place is in my pants.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Church songs with clapping... I don't think this is what Martin Presbyluther had in mind when he founded our religion by sticking his Three Suggestions under the Pope's windshield wiper.
Heyyyy.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Come on, Homer! I got an ambition to do some wishin'!
Um, Mr. Burns...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Come on, Homer. Tell him about the store. I'm dyin' out here.
Oh, there's the Frisbee.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Concussion... diddily... hemorrhage... doodily... injury... bodily...
Don't toy with me, woman.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Couldn't help overhearing, Simpson. I've got some ice-cold suds in the rumpus room, if you'd like to join me.
Relax. It's a "controlled burn"... Uh-oh.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Darn teenagers with their beer bottles.
What?! Why do I succeed at everything I audition for?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Dear Lord, I know you see all, but trust me, you do not want to see this.
This taser is awesome. Finally, a practical use for electricity.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Dear Lord, thank you for creating so many evil criminals for us to bring in. And also, thank you for my partner Homer, who...
Computer... kill Flanders.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Did I hear my name? My ears are burnin'.
Hii-hi-hi-hi, hi, Flanders. Go Wildcats!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Do you have a problem with the way I'm coaching?
Son of a bitch...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Do you reject Satan, and all his empty promises?
What is it, Flanders?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Do you think this looks okay?
Sorry son, I only have twenties. And if God needs money, why doesn't he just write another Bible? The first one sold pretty well.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Does anyone remember when it was considered rude to talk in church?
Mmm... soggy br--

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Don't say it, Homer. This is not the time.
I'm goin' home. It's not safe in here.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Don't use that dog as a ramp...
And I suppose you and Maude will be coming along as well?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Don't you think I've got better things to do on my honeymoon than spy on you two?
And didn't the Easter bunny himself say "forgive them, father, for finding all my eggs?" And if a giant rabbit can lay chocolate eggs, maybe you and Edna can find a way to make it work.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Edna, I had a long walk with Homer Simpson yesterday, and as I was carrying him back home, I had a lot of time to think.
Are your kids gonna be there?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Eh, for a little bit.
So, here's to my best friend, Ned.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Eh, well sir. My entire family is very touched and--
Ohh, don't worry, sweetheart, I'll get us the money. Even if I have to get a second job.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Evening, neighbor. Low on funds again?
...He had earned the nickname "Charlie Hustle...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Excuse me! With all this racket, my boys can't get their sixteen hours sleep.
Don't get me wrong, it's worth feeling three inches tall to find out what kind of a person you really are. Marge Simpson... President of the International We Love Flanders Fan Club...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Fee fi fo fum! I smell the potatoes au gratin of Marge Simp-son! Mmmm- mmm!
The hell with this!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Fella came into the store today and asked for change for a dollar. Well sir, I gave him three quarters by mistake. Took me the whole afternoon to track him down.
Who are you donating them to?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: First come, first served! What are you in for?
I loved you, man!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: For the last few weeks. But most of the time I've known you you've treated me like dirt!
What if we switched wives? Would that help?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: For the last time, no!
Listen, Flanders, do you still have that store?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: For two more days. Then it becomes Libertarian Party headquarters. I hope they have better luck than I did.
I know, and it doesn't get any easier from here. There's the Tongue-Kissing Festival... Cinco de Ocho... The Hobo Oscars... days just made for lovers. Not widowers, lovers.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Form of business? Sole proprietorship. "Owner's marital status?" Happily married... to a dead woman.
Fraid not infinity.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Fraid so infinity plus one.
The fly was funny and a booger was the icing on the cake...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Friends, we love you all, but I also have a "sinister" motive for asking you all here -- "sinister" being Latin for "left-handed." But enough joking.
Well, we tried all those other tools.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Gee, I always like to help you, Homer, but I don't want to be an accessory to some sort of shady doin's. And it does raise a whole host of ethical questions, such as...
Good-lookin' group.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Gee, looks like this town has a good Sam log-jam.
Okey-doke, let's hit the tables.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: God Homer, watching you risk your life turned my beat box all the way up to.. Rumba! Yea, I was praying you'd be safe but to be honest, part of me wanted to see ya get splattered.
A little cream?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Goes with the sugar!
I'm game if you are, Flanders.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Good gravy, what have I done?
What was that?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Greetings from Nedily Space Center on Cape Flandaveral. We noticed your sky-ro-technics and thought we'd join in. Ooh, looks like a perfect landing!
Flanders?! A perfect vacation ruined.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hate to be a needy Neddy, but, uh, could you do me a favor???
Go on...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: He taught us how to live a Burt Reynolds lifestyle on a Mac Davis income. We've already got tickets for his next seminar.
Marge, shh! It's important that no one know that I'm a food critic.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hear that, Maude? Homer's a critic.
Flanders, you saved me. Why?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Heck, you'd have done the same for me.
Language.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hell! Damn! Backside! Nothing matters anymore! I'm goin' down and my hand-basket seats two!
Deal. See, Flanders, you give a little, you get a little.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hello, "Mr. Brown Ground", whatcha got for me?
He came to life. Good for him.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Help me! Help me, Lord!
Just tucking him in.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Here you go, your rubber training knife. You've attained the rank of Pussy Willow.
All right, well that's okay. When they come to rescue him, they'll rescue us.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Here's our chance! Dolphins always help humans lost at sea.
Ahh... Is that a fact? And you think you know someone.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Here's our house... a rainbow... a white hand shaking a black hand...
You got that right. Throw on the mesquite, Bart!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Here, this may sound just a teensy bit insane in the ol' membrane, Homer. But I, I was wondering if you could show me how to have some fun.
Old Man Flanders!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey Homer! Sneakin' kisses from the Missus?
Hello there, Flan-didly-danders.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey Homer, I've been singing your praises all day. Marge said we could have choir practice in your house tonight.
Ohh, you son-of-a.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey Homer, Ya know, I owe you one, buddy. No sooner had I shaved off the old cookie duster, than a lady cast me in a commercial.
Noooo! Bart, that's a really bad storage area!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey Homer, why the sour puss? Didja chugalug a skunky Snapple?
CHRISTMAS IN DECEMBER / WOW WOW WOW / GIVE ME TONS OF PRESENTS / NOW NOW NOW!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey Homer, writing a new Christmas carol?
Hey... that's the same thing you said to Bart after he choked in that soccer game. And we both know he sucked.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey Marge, I don't I don't really want a computer. You know all those complete strangers Googling each other. Makes my flesh crawl.
Oh c'mon, stay for dessert!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey Simpson, you wanna hear about the big change in my life?
Oh, it feels so good to talk to another human being. Stupid Flanders.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, Homer, I need to ask ya a favor. My baby sitter canceled and I got tickets to a Christian rock concert.
But, I learned my lesson. It'll never happen again.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, Homer, what's the big brouhaha? Ha.
Interesting proposal. Now with an opposing point of view: bubbles.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, cool your jets! We're trying to get to sleep!
Hey... Hmm. Not bad. Nice hot mustard... good bread... Turkey's a little dry. The turkey's a little dry?! Oh foul, accursed thing! What demon from the depths of hell created thee?!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, fellow slave, is that one of those monkey paw dealies that lets you wish for things?
Yep. That's where they cook up their "vittles.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, here come the Simpsons. N-Now be careful, Homer. There's a fella in the sand right in front of ya...
Well, I've taken eight months off. It's time to get back on the horse.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, neighbor, your welcome mat's lookin' a little dusty.
Those feelings are normal, Ned. They're part of the process. Watch the sprinkler.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, that's my sprinkler.
Well, yeah.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, whatever happened to the plow from your old snowplow business?
Yeah, it'd be nice to entertain friends and have people over.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, you got a tennis court.
Sounds like goood watchin'.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey-hey there, Marge. Just brought the kids over to share a prayer with the blessed angel, if it's okay with you.
Marge, quit livin' in the past.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Heydilly ho, window buddy. Just wonderin' if you'd like to come over and give the new pool table a whirl.
I know, I know. I can still make this for five. Come on, baby, pleeze pleeze go in. Pleeze.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hi, Simpson! Having fun?
Flanders! Open up!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hi-de-ho-e-roonie, neighbor. What can I do you for?
And he's great with the neighbors.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hi-diddly-ho! There's "no bot" like a robot!
Don't hurt me! Here's my wallet.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hi-didly-ho, Schuss in Boots.
Happy New Year!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hi-ho pagans! New Years was three months ago, but here's a present anyhoo!
God, if you really are God, you'll get me tickets to that game.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hidilly ho, neighbor. Wanna go to the game with me? I got two tic...
Wait, let's just leave it on till we forget our troubles.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hm, sounds like a plan.
I engaged in intercourse with your spouse or significant other. Now that's psychiatry! Eh? Eh?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Ho ho ho. Very funny, wise guy.
Hello hotline? I am very tempted by another woman.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer Simpson! That's a dilly of a pickle. Hey, let's conference you with Marge, huh?
Bed goes up. Bed goes down. Bed goes up. Bed goes down. Bed goes up. Bed goes down. Bed goes up. Bed goes down.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer Simpson! Well, if that don't put the "dink" in co-inky-dink.
Everybody hear that?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer! Homer! It's a miracle!
Look at the size of that bird! I'd go Henry the Eighth on those drumsticks.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer! I can't believe you're partaking with my parents!
Ladies, we want to do the honorable thing. So breakfast is on us, with full waffle-bar privileges. But first, I'm afraid we have some bad news. The waffle bar is closed. I'm sorry. I'm so very--

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer! The bad news, ladies, is we already have wives.
Turn right here. I keep this frozen meat in case society collapses but we still have power.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer! This is my freezerino.
No sale.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, Christian life isn't all praying and sacrifice. Hey, dig this.
No, don't tell me, I'll get it... Oh, I know! The Lord is vengeful! O Spiteful One! Show me who to smite, and they shall be smoten!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, God didn't set your house on fire.
Hey Flanders, have you seen my Frisbee?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, I can foretell people's deaths!
Well? What did everybody think?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, I can honestly say that was the best episode of Impy and Chimpy I've ever seen.
So, how 'bout a little stakeout music?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, I don't think we have the same musical tastes.
Helen, as a responsible parent, I was already well aware of that.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, I'm as permissive as the next parent. I mean, just yesterday, I let Todd buy some Red Hots with a cartoon devil on the box. But you can't possibly think it's appropriate for your ten-year-old son to work in a burlesque house!
Hiya, Flanders! Oooh... dinner! May I join you?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, I-I'd love to chitty-chat, but tonight's the night I do my charity work.
Just warming it up. Now to melt the cheese in this croissant...and get rid of a little excess earwax...and smoke a relaxing cigar.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, can we take it easy on the taser?
People here do not respect boundaries.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, did you just buckle your belt through my loop?
Oh my God, this dude does the best Flanders! You got the mustache and the didilly... Okay, now do Wiggum.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, i-i-it's me, Ned.
Okay, remember where we parked.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, is that my muffler?
C'mon, man. What's the catch?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, just call me a little bubble 'cause I'm on the level. Punch me.
Ned, if it's boneheaded to talk you outta seein' Edna, then I don't wanna be brainheaded.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, listen to me. For a long time now I've been lookin' over the fence at that wonderful relationship you have with Marge. Then I remember what it was like to have a sweet woman of my own lying in a twin bed across the hall from mine.
C'mon! We've been here for fifteen minutes. Can't you see they're sucking the life out of us?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, maybe you'd have had more fun at Moe's tonight.
Oh, wait. I left a sandwich in there.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, no! You promised... Everything was supposed to be by the book!
Flanders? Kill me? You never killed anybody... and you're gonna start with the big dog?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, please, don't tempt the gods. I-I mean God! There's-there's one God! Only one! Well, sometimes there's three.
Flanders, that stuff's been here for thousands of years. But the breakfast buffet at this hotel, which is included in our package, closes in ten minutes!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, that's not why we're here. We can see the stations of the cross!
...and your infinite patience with a big, dumb jerk like me. Oh, Ned, I don't deserve you as a neighbor, but will you forgive a young, handsome fool and come home?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, that's really touching. But my boys and I are trying to make a new start, and the people here are a little more my cup of...
You mean Lisa?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, they blew that up yesterday.
Whuh?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, this is the most sacred spot in Christendom, not your backyard hammock.
Then I insist on walking you home.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, this really isn't necessary...
I have some adjustments to make.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, when am I gettin' my power drill back?
Are you sure? Oh, rats. No offense, Sweetie.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, why don't we go make the girls some custom omelettes?
This case is "in the bag.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, you could've killed him!
Now, we'll just send this to the dating service, the chicks'll fall for you, and bam! The healing begins.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, you obviously went to a lot of trouble, but dating? It just feels way too soon.
Why don't I just put on a dress?!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, you've met my parents.
Like a woman who's made the biggest mistake of her life.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer? What are you doing here?
Welly, welly, welly... Mr. Clean wants to hang with Dirty Dingus Magee.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: How 'bout it, Homer? Will you teach me the secret of your intoxicating lust for life?
Okay, let's go boating!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: How are my boys doin', Homer?
Ginger throws Ned a kiss.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: How are we going to get outta this mess in an honorable and decent--
Well, there you go. Now how 'bout a drink?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: How do you do it, Homer? How do you silence that little voice that says, "Think"?
Just be happy with what you got, son. Don't try to keep up with the Flanderses.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: How do you like my new wheels, Simpson?
Boy, that'd be sweet.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Howdy-do, neighbor! Good pipe weather. Thought I'd fire up the briar.
C'mon, all the teens on bikes are doin' it.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Howdy-do, strangers! Hop on in before you become a couple runneth over!
Ohh, she wants to have coffee sometime.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I can hear her, Homer.
It's El Flanderito! Run him down!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I can't run, I'm wearing flip-flops!
What did I do?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I can't say for sure, but as a Christian, I assume the worst.

Because when you get down to it, aren't all religions the same? They tell you what to eat, when to pray... how this imperfect clay that we call man can mold itself to resemble the divine. But we can never attain that ultimate grace while there is hatred in our hearts for each other.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I did it! I reached him!
Who undid my do?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I didn't do diddily, and certainly not squat!
Flanders!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I don't blame you for being upset with me, Homer. I just wanted to give you this letter. I'll leave now.
Flanders? I don't know... I mean, you haven't done anything for me since you lent me that five thousand bucks yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I don't claim to be the perfect neighbor...
She's just like Clark Kent. When there's lots of excitement, she's nowhere to be found. Nighty-night, sweetie.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I don't know, neighboreenos, I'm all for Halloween fun, but a séance sounds a little PG-13.
Yeah, isn't this place great? If you're single you can come here every night.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I don't wanna come here. Last time I did, someone slipped me a Mickey and wrote "CHURCHY JOE" on my face.
What have you done to my family?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I figured a good time to pick you up was when they were at Lisa's recital.
You hang onto resentment like a Confederate widow.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I forgave you for accidentally killing my wife.
Honey, I couldn't keep 'em away if I tried. Except for Flanders. He was mysteriously called out of town.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I got your letter, Jesus and I'm coming as fast as I can.
But ice cream cake...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I gotta find Homer -- he's gonna blow up the whole town!
You see, Ned... your city-wide nagging compressed all of our town's misbehavior into one small place...creating a glittering diamond of super evil.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I guess I did create this... like God created the devil.
Oh man, this is long. Could you read it to me?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I guess that could be arranged.
It's natural to feel that way, but the sprinkler is gone. It's time to let go.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I just bought that...
Okay, be right down.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I just keep replaying the whole thing in my head. I can't believe my last words to Maude were "No foot-longs.
Whaat?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I just this minute bought it at the hardware st...
Fine. Keep 'em. But you have to give back... Lisa?!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I just thought if we got together we could change the channel from "The Feud Network" to "Comity Central.
Well, I like A.C.-D.C.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I like their Christian cover band: A.D.-B.C.! KINDLY DEEDS / DONE FOR FREE / KINDLY DEEDS
Yeah, but you hold onto the big things! The point is, the more I got to know you, the more I got to like you.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I like you too, but you broke the law. So I've got to bring you in.
The first meeting of "Hell's Satans" is called to order.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I move we reconsider our club name. Make it something a little less blasphemous. After all we don't want to go to Hell.
Flanders?! Can't a man just drink alone on a Wednesday morning?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I need your advice. It's about a lady.
God created the devil? Finally, He did something cool.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I never wanted to turn into Big Brother. I just wanted to be Little Sister, tattlin' on everyone so the town would be a nicer place.
Ahh, precious memories.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I okeley dokely shmokely do!
Huh?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I should box your ears you, you, you... You Sneaky Pete!
It's best to concentrate on what you do have.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I started drinking orange juice with pulp! I asked the Reverend and he said it was okay. Then he hung right up on me. That man is cranky at three in the mornin'.
And you are how old?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I suppose, if you must know... I'm... well, I'm... I'm sixty.
Well, aren't you gonna invite me in?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I sure appreciate you folks offering to go through Maude's things. If it were up to me, I wouldn't throw anything away.
I don't have time for that.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I think I'm gonna be sick.
Looks like you're missing a wife.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I walked right into that one.

dialogue.text: The Bible says "cast your bread upon the waters." But all I got was a bunch of soggy bread.

dialogue.text: This one's mine. And this one's mine. This one's mine... and this--

dialogue.text: Uh, Homer, I think you want your house, next door.
