dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, something's in there all right.
Dear Homer, I.O.U. one emergency donut. Signed, Homer. Bastard. He's always one step ahead. Oh, I'd sell my soul for a donut!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, that can be arranged.
No, I wanna make you a respecting stock. I don't know if you've noticed, but I've borrowed a lot of your stuff over the years...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, that is true. In fact--
My demons and I are closer than ever. Next year we're gonna visit every major league baseball park. I'm just goin' in to bust Marge out.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, that's good too, I guess.
That's right, it's my sad duty to rat out this man for defrauding a car wash. How, you ask? With a phony senior discount card!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, that's not quite true--
Maybe.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, the Bible says it's fun to do stuff together.
Yes, but this time I'm sober. Ish.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, the hobos sure will appreciate our old clothes and lima beans.
Oh, Flanders, I, uh, want to give you your stuff back.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, there's no house to put it in, Homer, not since that nice fellow from the bank, who was only doing his job, came and locked it up.
And would they pay handsomely for the privilege?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, they might. But you'd have to be awfully money-grubbing to charge your friends and neighbors...
How many "s"'s in "innocent"?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, tippity-top o' the a.m. to every-good-body here! As chairman of the PTA, I Am dee-diddily-lighted to take over, and I think I can put the "pal" back in principal.
Exactly. It came to me in a vision. Or maybe it was a drunken haze. Or, possibly, an ice cream headache.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, well, well, looks like someone's having a pre-Rapture party.
Flanders, what's your secret? You never get arrested, you don't buy your clothes at "Mr. Blob" and look at your beautiful lawn. It sickens me.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, whatever I've got I owe to hard work, honest living, and flossing my teeth, tail and toes. Plus a little prayer now and then.
I'll steal it back when you're sleep-ing.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, when the sun goes down it means God's gone to China to watch over those good folks. Time for some shuteye.
Beautiful! And star-wipe, aaaand we're out.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, with triple word score, that's ninety! Ha-ha, I guess my luck is starting to even out.
Oooh! Oooh! How much? How much? How much?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, you know they're not givin' 'em away. But sometimes you've just got to spoil yourself.
There's nothing wrong with crabgrass! It just has a bad name, that's all. Everyone would love it if it had a cute name like... uh... elfgrass.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, you may be right!
Maybe. We don't know that for sure.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, you've gotta take it back!
We should be bounty hunters together. You're kind and smart, I'm cruel and strong. Together, we're nothing. But together, we're the perfect bounty hunter.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well... I could use money. But you have to promise me something, Homer.
Anyway, over torture, one of your soldiers mentioned that you collect giant wooden animals. We hope you don't have a horse.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well... I don't have one from you!
Yeah. I missed her like five times.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: What a charming single entendre. Now look, I know marriage is scary, but if you really think she's the one, it gives you two a shot at forever.
Geez, I've never seen anyone so whipped so fast.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: What are we gonna do, Homer? My kids are gonna be traumatized! And then there's Maude. And then there's Maude!
Ohhh, so you're gonna welch on our bet?!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: What are you talking about? Neither boy lost.
Would you rather tell Maude the truth?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: What did the aliens look like?
Oh come on now, Flanders, I don't complain about your your... moustache.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: What's wrong with my moustache?
Fine. You're mad. What are you gonna do about it?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: When the month is up, I want you out!
Now if you could make with some bacon and eggs, I'll be on my way.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Why don't you come on in and have breakfast with us?
Flanders, I am a patient, reasonable, handsome man. But even I have my limits. Now beat it!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Why thank you, Homer. It's a popsicle in my favorite flavor -- plain.
D'OH D'OH D'OH D'OH D'OH D'OH D'OH / WOO WOO WOO WOO WOO WOO HOO / STU STU STU STU-PID FLANDERS...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Why the crescendo, my dear old friend-o?
Well, before she died, she ordered this Bible especially for you.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Why, there's my name in gold.
Oh, I was just driving around the mid-Atlantic states, ringin' doorbells at random, and I just... oh, who am I fooling with my awesome lies? I want you to come back to Springfield.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Why? So you can make me a laughingstock again?
But Amber, I can change!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Will you shut up?
I wish -- we were bicycling to a lake.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Wordplay: never cared for it. But it's never too soon for you two to join the "I do" crew. Now I'm not sayin' it's all Jell-O with Cool Whip. She'll nag ya. She'll try to change ya. You'll be fighting the same basic fight for years and years and years--
That is going right on stupidflanders.org.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Y'know, Homer, you might really benefit from opening your heart to the spirituality of this place. Please, neighbor?
I'm having problems with my new boss Roz. She's the most evil person to come out of Ohio since LeBron, but at least he thought long and hard before screwing everybody over, in public for no reason.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Y'know, I knew a backstabbin' buckeye named Roz at Bible Camp. Twice as tall as she should've been.
Well, well, well. So flawless Flanders needs help from stinky-pants Simpson.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yeah, I, I guess I do.
Ned, let's cut to the chase.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yeah, let me guess. You're probably gonna do something boneheaded like try to talk me outta seein' Edna.
You wear a bathing suit in the bathtub?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yeah, so I can't see my own shrinky dink.
Oh, yeah? Wanna bet?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yeah, well, I'm not a betting man.
Hey, Flanders, bad day at the rat races?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yeah. A crazy guy shot a bunch of people and the subway ran over my hat.
Flanders. Eh, I guess you've got some late night problems too.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yeah. I made a great film, but I'm havin' trouble gettin' it out there. I'm like Michael Moore, except I'm skinny, my jeans are washed, and God loves me. I just wish I could find some way to spread my message.
Ahh, you got lucky, Flanders! And fix that hat!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yeah. Thanks for the tip, Homer...
Flanders!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yep, I'm just replacing the front window at my store, which was broken in the riot.
Sara Sloane? The movie star?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yep. Why would that Twinkie want to go out with a ding dong like me?
This really means a lot to you, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yes, but it means more to you.
Ned, are you okay?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yes... but my mower can't get much lower!
I'm almost done.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You are a picture and a half! Well -- hee hee! -- if you're finished by tomorrow, come on over and strap on the feed bag. We're gonna fire up old Propane Elaine and put the heat to the meat! Nummy nummy num!
So you want Maggie to infect your kids?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You betcha! In fact, some parents have been known to hold "pox parties," so other kids in the neighborhood can get the disease when they please.
What are you buying? Jerk stuff?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You betcha! This kiosk sells personalized movies. I had one made starring little Rod.
I think my leg is broken.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You betcha. It's a nice break from the male sports I usually watch.
He took the time to press the shift key, Marge! I think he knows what he's talking about.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You get my boys tattoos, you change their school, you buy Rod sneakers that light up like Times Square...shoes are shoes and lights are lights! Now, just when do I get a say in how my boys are raised?! This marriage isn't perfect!
Better yet, you have to mow my lawn in your wife's Sunday dress.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You have yourself a bet, you jackaninny!
Hello! Hello? Anybody home? Hello?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You jumped bail, Homer. I gotta bring you in.
I know!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You know at times like these, I-I used to turn to the Bible and find solace. But even the good book can't help me now.
I guess I'm more powerful than God now.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You know what they say: "With great power comes great responsibility.
Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me but weep for yourselves.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You know, Homer's givin' it the old bible college try. Maybe I should have dialed down the Doubting Thomas.
Oh.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You know, ever since that barbecue, nothing's gone right. It's like there's been a-a curse on me.
I'll tell you what's over! This partnership!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You know, if you take your foot off the accelerator going downhill, you wouldn't use so much gas.
Boy, what's this world coming to?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You know, that's exactly what I --
No, it isn't.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You must have something you want to wish for, Homer.
Okay. Flanders, you see...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You soft-core sophomores took advantage of my trustful nature. And sullied the internet by putting pornography on it!
Oh, wake up, Ned. You think Maude isn't dating in heaven?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You think she would?
Oh, that. That can be treated with our good friend alcohol. You might want to write that down. Where the hell's your notebook?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You threw it out the...
But, there is one condition...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You wanna hit me. Well sir, here's a roll of quarters to put in your fist for extra punching power!
How 'bout a Greg Norman Executive Putter from the Sky Mall?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You'd probably get a better deal at a mall back home.
WAY HEAL AWAY! / WE'LL HEAL AWAY JOE!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You're never bored paintin' the Lord.
Hey, Marge, surf's up!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You're using my table saw to violate a court order?
Mr. Flanders, how did you make these amazing fish?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Actually, God made some fish that were pretty close to these, so naturally we selected those for further breeding.
Hi.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: And it wouldn't hurt you to put up some curtains.
And they read Newsweek instead of nothing.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: C'mon, you Gloomy Gusses. Who's up for a big bowl of non-fat ice milk?
Mr. Flanders, why are you moving?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Cause I had a vision of myself... shooting your father.
Mr. Flanders, with all due respect, Bart didn't do anything.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Do I hear the sound of butting in? It's gotta be little Lisa Simpson -- Springfield's answer to a question no one asked!
Well, you can't fight fate, but if you must shoot our father, please remember our family motto: "Not in the face.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Don't worry, sweetie. I am not going to kill your father.
Hi, Mr. Flanders, I see you're reading the newspaper.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Everything but the opinion page! I don't need to be told what to think... by anyone living!
Four queens! Yes! Yes!!!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Gambling, eh? Satan's most potent recruiting tool!
I got it.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Good luck, Homer. No hard feelin's.
That came from Baboon County, U.S.A.!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Help! What do I do?!
Dad, hide your shame!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey Homie, I can see your doodle!
Sorry, Daddy.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, heard some no-goodnik stole your tree. Well we got a 30 footer, so you can have the top of ours.
Yeah. It seems like our house, but everything's got a creepy Pat Boone-ish quality to it.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, kids! Nachos, Flanders-style! That's cucumbers with cottage cheese.
Fine. I'll play outside.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, why that sounds like Gabriel's trumpet. You know what that means, kids?
Ah! Ah! Ah! Stop! Stop!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hmm. I seem to have mashed more hair into it. Oh well.
I don't get it. Straight A's, perfect attendance, Bathroom Timer... I should be the most popular girl in school.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, I'm in a rhubarb of a pickle of a jam here. I was all set to go off on vacation, when I get called up for jury duty. Oh, it's a corker of a case -- seems a man drove up onto a traffic island and hit a decorative rowboat full of geraniums.
But... but I'm very mature for my age. People often mistake me for nine.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, I've got a fozzie of a bear of a problem. Y'know, Maude and her mother were visiting Tyre and Sidon, the twin cities of the Holy Land. They must've kneeled in the wrong place and prayed to the wrong God, because, well, they're being held prisoner by militants of some sort.
But Dad, it defeats the purpose if you're powering our windmill with the electricity from Flanders.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, this meeting of your "fan club" is adjourned!
Oh, Bart, cartoons don't have to be one hundred percent realistic.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Howdilly hey, Camper Bart. Ready for today's meeting?
Well, it looks like everything worked out just fine for everybody.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Huh, credit card bill seems a little chunky this month.
Can you sign my yearbook?!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I'm glad the only beef between us is this burger!
Zap! Zap! Zap! Zap! Zap! Zap! I curse you, Hell's Kitten!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Just as I feared: her Buddhism has led directly to witchcraft.
Nice try, Dad.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Just hold your horses, son. Hey, hey, Simpson.
No, Dad! I think there's a leak in the line.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Leak in the line?
You mean Hawaii?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Mm-hm. That's the one! They've got a top-notch leper colony there, so we shipped 'em right off. Ooh, cost us a bundle, too. I guess we'll have an "Imagination Christmas" this year.
We've only brought in five dollars. And that came from Mr. Flanders buying back his own stuff.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: My LP of "Dreamcoat!
Hey, I'm a Buddhist!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: My Satan sense is tingling! Into the root cellar, boys!
Heh, you're not really giving my father power of attorney, are you?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Of course I... Oh, my stars! I can't do that.
But we heard them hovering!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh ho, I'm afraid I played a dirty part in this little charade.
Are there at least games here?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh no, "Games" stands for Gathering of American Messengers for Evangelical Sports!
How about asking the community for donations?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Ohhh, I'm not very good at begging people for stuff.
I warned ya. And yet my punishment is no less severe. That's odd.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Springfield is rife with the seven deadly sins! Starting with... GLUTTONY!
Boycott Funzo. He's a toy-killing machine!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: That shy little imp?
I'll do it! I'll babysit!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, I don't know, Lisa. You're awfully young, and the boys can be a handful. Todd's been pinching everyone lately.
I just don't think religion should be taught in our schools, any more than you'd want scientists teaching at the church.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, I wish this world would evolve a few more kids like you, Lisa.
After all, what civilized person would play a game with the skin of an innocent pig?!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, actually, Lisa, these balls are synthetic.
We give up.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, guess! Book of Revelations... Fire-breathing lion's head... tail made out of snakes... Who else is it gonna be?!
This is where I live.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, hello! It's one of those music industry superstars who's turning our innocent children into ladies of the night.
Because the myth of Jebediah has value, too. It's brought out the best in everyone in this town. Regardless of who said it, "a noble spirit embiggens the smallest man.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, hey, it's Homer! Good to see ya, neighb--
Nothing is going to happen, Mom. I hate to disappoint you, but the world is not coming to an end.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, shall we sing a hymn? Uh, "Nearer My God to Thee", maybe? Or, or, or "Amazing Grace"?
That's right. A girl wants to play football. How about that?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, that's super-duper, Lisa! In fact, we already have four girls on the team.
But I'm smart and responsible, and my parents will be right next door!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, what do you say, Homer? Can Lisa babysit for my kids?
Mr. Flanders, where's your store?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well... I'm down to a kiosk, thanks to that place.
My scalp hurts from horsefly bites.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Why don't you freeze it with an ice cube and hit it with a hammer? Works for me when I get bubbly-gum in the ol' push-broom.
Didn't you hear I almost killed my brother?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You did? Just a minute. What time can you come over?
It looks like a human skeleton... but these other bones look almost like wings.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You mean like... an angel?!!
So that "natural selection" was the origin of this species?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yup, that's exactly... Oh, you almost got me.
Not one that I want the public to see.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: ... So recycling is our way of giving Mother Earth a great big hug.
Please Homie, don't hurt him!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: ...and a backrub can just be a backrub. It doesn't have to lead to adult situations.
Mm-hmm.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Ahh, of course! This must be where he dropped the dagger. And this is the butler's pantry where Mrs. Astor concealed herself. And right here's where they found the torso heap! In front of our very own fireplace!
That's it. We have to get them back to school.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: All right, I'd like to call this meeting of the PTA to or-diddly-order and let's see if we can't put an end to this strike fuss, huh? Mrs. Krabappel, why don't you begin?
Keep yelling, you big ape.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Aren't you being a little hard on old Homie?
Ned! Maude! You've got to go back to your house. Something incredible has happened!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Aw, what happened now? Did the rubble burn down?
Enough with the voting. Ned, Edna, why didn't you tell us?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Cause everyone in this town makes such a big heckabaloo out of everything.
Yes, God.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Doggone it, Eve, I think you'd better hightail it outta this Garden!
The father of the loser mows the lawn --

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Eh, eh, just a minute. "Loser" is such a harsh word. Couldn't we just say "the boy who doesn't win"?
Ned, how did you sleep?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Fine, I guess. Thanks for loaning me your pajamas, Homer. And Marge, thank you for those helpful chip bag clips.
Shoo! Shoo!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Heaven and earth... Where were we? Oh, now I'm lost.
No Rudner.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Here are the numbers for the police, fire, ambulance, poison control, burn clinic, and people nearby with Rod and Todd's blood type.
I'll twist this bottle in your face...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Here, Marge, let me. Hate to be an armchair Blanche, but I always gave it one of these...
This story is as dark as those new Milky Way bars. Ooh, that's a good analogy. I'll work it in somewhere. But now I need some romance, pronto!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey Marge, you look like you could use a nice big stud... detector.
Uh, I don't want to judge the rightness of your ego orientation, but my inner critic says you should've done your job!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey now, Marge. Let's not "should" this fella to death.
It's a snuggle dungeon!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, Homer, can I get back my...
Wish I could get a little of that attention.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, Simpsons! Don't mean to be a pesto, but I'll be happy to watch your scampy shrimp.
Children! Go!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, anybody mind if I serve as bartender? You know, I have a Ph.D in Mixology.
We had a lot of fun. They're terrific kids.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, you're welcome to see the dynamic duo any time.
But small. Really, really small.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hm. Wh-when you put it that way, it does seem a bit small.
You are not pretending to be dead, young lady. This family has had nothing but bad luck when it comes to farce.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, it's Neddy. I baked you a little something to ease the pain.
Homer!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Howdy, Homer. You here for a viewin' of my shampooin'?
Rachel Jordan? Isn't that the woman you had a crush on, Ned?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I didn't have a "crush" on her.
I'm sorry, Ned. I never thought this would happen.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I don't want you watching my boys ever again!
Some people would call it "cozy.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I guess it is sorta cute...
Ned, I know you like to worry, but these boys are never going to get self-confidence unless you let them try things for themselves.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I just can't. They're all I've got since that sad day when Maude found eternal happiness.
Homer!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I kinda figured this might happen, so I built the shelter big enough for both our families.
Now, Ned, troubled boys need rules and discipline. They crave it! You just lay down the law.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I know, but... they're on their mini-bikes and all...
Ned, there's only one man I should be eating whipped cream with.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I never thought otherwise.
Ned, are you checking up on me?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I'm not Ned, I'm a friendly dog. Oh, I'm not a good liar. I did come here to check on the... where's Rod?
Oh, can you sing it again?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I'm sorry, it really was one of those spur-of-the-moment-type things.
What is it, Ned?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I've got two teens in a public park goin' at it like a couple of gibbons in the back seat of Noah's Ark!
Christmas card? I haven't even taken the photo yet!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Isn't this your posse on this glossy?
We have to get out of here!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: It was people. People soiled our green!
Remarkable -- there doesn't seem to be any damage at all. It just goes to show you that everything will work out if you have faith.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: It's all gone. Everything... gone-diddily-on.
It's a miracle!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: It's almost like she's alive again.
Homer! Do something about the noise!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: It's seven a.m. What are they cock-a-doodily-doin'?
I can't wait to see what evolution will make next: maybe a bird with a people face, or a bear with pants on!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Let's go, boys. Your poor old Popsicle's been licked.
Forget about him. Let's rehearse the bottle scene!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Let's not and say we did.
Milhouse, stop that!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Little higher, Wendell... A lot higher, Martin... Ah, Ralph, that's a basketball.
I'm so sick of Gil... he ruins Thanksgiving... uses my leg razor to peel his carrots...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Marge, I hate to interrupt the ol' solilo-diddly-iloquy, but I just want to thank you for your early Christmas card.
Ned Flanders, I can't believe you struck my husband.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Marge, I've been racked with guilt and pain... my moustache fell out! This is a clip-on!
Don't you defend him! I want that mooch out of my house right now!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Marge, I've never seen you like this before.
All right! I admit it -- they're both at the Catholic Church! Reverend, what should I do?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Marge, this calls for an emergency meeting of the church's spiritual council. To Stuckey's!
Should we inform the Chief?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Maybe. But I feel a little like I'm the Tom Voyeur to these Huckleberry Sinners.
And Ned, I haven't seen you this happy in years.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Mm-hmm. I haven't felt this good since we stole the 2000 election.
I'm sorry, Ned. Looks like God has packed up and left Springfield.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: No, no, you're lying! You're lying! What makes you lie?
But Ned, saying nay is your thing.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Not this month! Edna signed us up for a tango class. It was the only way I could avert wine tasting.
Oh my. Ned's next movie seems even bloodier than the last one.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Now, there's no need to actually whip 'em. We can put the sound in later.
That Photoshopping freak!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh I don't mean to cause Gil ill will, but still...
You stole this entire room from Ned Flanders' house!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh well, you snooze you lose. But uh, can I have my photo albums back?
Ned! Where are you?!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, I can't see the name of the station... but the gas costs one forty-nine and eight tenths.
Ned, let me give you a little something for babysitting.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, I can't take money from a neighbor. Although, business at the Leftorium's been pretty slow since that big chain store came to town.
Ned, there's more to the Bible than blood and gore.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, I-I guess you'd rather see a film about a liberal European wizard school, or the latest sexcapade of Miss Ashley Judd!
That's ridiculous. Homer's not dead, he's right out back in the hammock.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, Marge. Of course Homer's alive. He's alive in all our hearts.
Hello? Anyone home?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, hi, Marge. Heh-heh. Guess we gave you quite a start. We were painting Todd's room red -- pretty messy work -- and then we came out here to take a break. Must've dozed off.
Hi, Ned. I didn't know you were an actor.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, indeedily-doodily. I've even been in "Streetcar" once before. I played Blanche DuBois! Hmmm huh. Just part of the fun of going to an all-male school.
I'll call you back! Come back, Pooter Toot! People might be offended by your mild tastelessness!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, isn't that a cute little choo-choo...
First Communion?!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, we've gotta stop 'em now! Once they seal the deal, there's no turning back. Like the Jews with their snippity-snip.
Mmmm. Goodbye, Ned. If the slightest thing goes wrong with that house, I want you to call me right away. Or you can beep me. In fact, why don't you just stay here tonight? We'll go to a hotel.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, you're sweet to offer, but, uh, we're all just so tired, we just want to get to our new house and rest in peace.
Oh, Ned! I'm so sorry!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh-ho-ho. No problem, Marge. Oh.
Ned, to make up for what happened, I want to invite you and the boys over to dinner tomorrow night.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Okily-dokily. But I'm warning you, you're gonna see America's number-one dishwashing crew!
So who wants to play a game? Hmm? Hmm? Hmm?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oo, that's a noodle scratcher.
No. I'm fine. I'm going to my sisters' now.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Ooh, careful there, Marge! Almost nicked me!
What do you think, Maggie?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Ooh, wow, it's the Big Unit himself, Randy Johnson! You've fanned more men than Salome!
Oh my God! Dinner with Burly!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Playing a prankeroo, eh?
Don't listen to them, Maggie. Maggie?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Please change me back! This bumble bee has developed an unhealthy obsession with me.
It's Bart!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Pray for a miracle, boy! God can hear you better from up there!
Stop it, stop it. Can't you see this barnyard noise guessing game is tearing us apart?!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: QUE SERA, SERA / WHATEVER WILL BE, WILL BE...
Well, we thought we'd wait a little while.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Really? Not married? And you were bicycling two abreast?
Street signs? Indoors?! Whatever.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Rod, you order anything you want for your big ten-oh.
You'd be surprised what he could do if you just gave him a chance.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Rod... You can do it, boy! With God on your side, you can't fail!
Dinner's ready! Dinner's ready!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Saved by the bell from eternity in Hell!
... some ice cream at the store, since I'm saving so much money on diet cola.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Say your prayers, Simpson...

God's plan?! God isn't some video gamer up there controlling us like we were pac men and dig dugs! God isn't Sky Police. God didn't do this. I lied to my husband, and made my kids lie too! We did this.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: She's right. We thought we could enter the den of sin and emerge unscathed. But we were scathed! Those free ginger ales at the casino... I didn't declare them on my taxes!
Um, how long have you two been married?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Since two this afternoon. Welcome to our honeymoon!
Ned! You bought our house? Why?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: So I can rent it back to you. Just pay what you can till you get back on your feet.
BUT WE'RE HAPPY JUST THE WAY WE ARE!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: THEY'RE NOT PERFECT, BUT THE LORD SAYS LOVE THY NEIGHBOR --
Bake sale -- taken... candle snuffing -- taken... baby shusher, miscellaneous choir support -- everything's taken! All that's left is...

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Teen abstinence counseling! You get to pass out abstinence pledges and make sure the kids sign their John Han-bleeps.
That was a very nice thing you did, Homey.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Thank you. Thank you so much, Homer. You really are a you're a true friend.
No. There is absolutely nothing else to tell you about this house.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: That's good enough for me.
We're not gonna make it!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Tonight's G-rated gem is a silent film from my favorite year -- yester! And while you enjoy this quiet riot, I'll be slipping these religious pamphlets on your windshields.
Hello. Listen Lady.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Uh, I'm in some hot soup here, Marge. Uh, some teenagers are hanging out in front of the store. I... I think they could start slacking at any moment.
Hello. Listen Lady.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Uh, Marge, I... I appreciate your advice, but, uh, things have gotten... Well, they... they're a lot worse.
I'm glad you're not mad, but I lied to you! And I won't feel right until I return your deposit.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: We appreciate the offer, Marge, but I think we're going to be very happy here.
Ned Flanders, I can't believe what you doodily-did for us.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well sir, as the ocean said to the dirt, I appreciate the sediment.
Ned, that's so generous. But there must be something I could do in return.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well sir, we could do a little Quid Pro for the Kay-Pro. The left-handed convention is in town, and as the owner of Springfield's largest southpaw shop, I just gotta be there. Could you uh, nanny-goat my kid-diddly-ids?
She's not a devil. I just don't know what to do.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, Christmas is coming, huh?
This is the worst thing you've ever done.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, Ginger, sure is, uh, um, neat that you managed to hunt me down.
But this is your chance to contact your late wife, Maude.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, I do miss the Mrs...
Ned's letting us use his freezer to store the extra sandwiches.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, I felt a little guilty for taking back what belonged to me.
Oooh, hot comes out of hot... it's like I'm dreaming! Thank you, Ned.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, I guess I'd better be...
Ned, Homer and I are a little concerned with the way the school's being run.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, I may go a little bit easy on the old hickory dickory stick, but that's, that's because my dad was so hard on me when I was a boy.
Oh, thanks.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, I'd better skedaddle. Oh, there's one more weensy little thing -- you see that tree over there?
I'm sorry, Mr. Hutz, but I just can't lie to people.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, I'm just gonna spill my guts: I love it to death! I'm gonna give you a deposit this minute.
Ned! I think we have a gas leak!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, I'm sorry, I just had my glass of warm milk which means I am closed for business!
Ned please, you're our guest.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, actually... as your landlord, repairs are my responsibility. I'll just get my tools...
Ned, I'm not afraid!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, aren't you a super-duper recouper.
Um... Do you have time to look at a few other leaks, faulty wires and dangerous mold conditions?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, as you are my tenants, I'll see what I can do.
You've got a big house, Ned. If you need extra money, why don't you rent out a room?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, it might be fun to be a landlord. Landfella -- there's only one Lord!
Ned, I'm worried about you. You've been working non-stop for the past week.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, it's been a tad harder than I thought, but I'm not complaining 'cause I work for a sweet, sweet, boss. You're our foreman, Maude.
Just hope the kids didn't hear us.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, maybe your kids didn't.
Ned, we meant well, and everyone here tried their best --

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, my family and I can't live in good intentions, Marge! Oh, your family is out of control, but we can't blame you, because you have goooood intentions.
Because it's so dilapidated.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, nothing's perfect, I sure hate to make you come out here and not buy a house.
Ned, that's so considerate.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, some say being thoughtful is old-fashioned. If so, then I guess I'm just a cave man. If they existed, which they didn't!
Everything's covered in foam. And it's owned by a corporation, so you know it's safe.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, their mascot is a kneepad wearing a helmet... why not?
No, I had to go rent the bulldozer.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, we all changed our minds.

There must be something else. Think Marge, think. Culture... vulture... birds of prey... pray in a church... the father, son and Holy Ghost... ghosts are scary, scary rhymes with Gehry! That's it -- Architect Frank Gehry! He could build us a concert hall like he did in Los Angeles.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, we could use a new H.Q. for the Springfield Philharmonic. They're playing Gustav Mahler in abject squalor.
Mm. That sounds perfect!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, what the heck. Who's ready to build an amusement park?
It's fun to cook dinner together. Homer and I never do it anymore. Cook together, that is.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: What's the next task on the old i-dinnerary?
genie.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: When I was putting new insulation in your attic, I slipped on this lamp and really banged my head.
Disguises? I'm worried that our scam is becoming dishonest.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Why, I bet the Lord is pleased as punch that we're using that dirty casino money to rebuild his temple. Our mission is one hundred percent pure.
So, did anyone see that new Woodsy Allen movie?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Y'know, I like his films, except for that nervous fella who's always in 'em.
Are you okay, Ned?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yeah, just a little shocked. What's that? Some kinda sorting machine?
Well, Ned, you don't have to stand for that. You just march right up to those youngsters and tell them to vamoose.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yeah, well, if you're sure that'll help...
Ned Flanders, you would take our family to the Holy Land just to try to make my husband a better man?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yep. I also want to try something called "pita bread.
I'm afraid handholding isn't going to cheer me up.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yes, but Jesus said that... pretty much the same thing. Darnit, the Bible said the Devil would be attractive!
See, see what I'm dealing with here, Ned? We invited them here, and they repay us with insults and judgments.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Yes, but there's two sides to every--
It's impossible. I killed you.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You can't kill the undead, silly.
Well, some general-interest magazines would be nice.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You got it, Eve.
Great stuff, Ned.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You know I was gonna enter this here Ovenfresh Bakeoff... but up against you, I wouldn't have a Hindu's chance in Heaven.
I just think when two people disagree, the big jerk ought to apologize.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You know Marge, Maude and I had a fight right before she died...
They started it!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You saved me, Reverend. You really went above and beyond. Thank you!
Homer, it'll just be a few minutes more!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You're a dame and I'm a fella.
Hi Ned. Where are the boys?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: oh, they're grounded. I found out Rod watched a commercial for "Grey's Anatomy," and Todd took a full day to tell me.
Oh, how I envy the crotchless.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: And this is where sinners spend all of eternity!
A satellite? What do we do? What do we do?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Discotheques," "Frat Houses," "Malibu." Nothing about satellite fires!
The rest of our lives.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Gosh, fifty thousand dollars? I'm donating this whole check to "Bibles for Belgians.
College boy.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Hey, Homer! Care to try some of my Flanders Planters punch?
Are you kiddin'? Homer's the one what wised us up to the sexy goin's on.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, is this true?
Hey, hey, I may be ugly and hate-filled, but I, uh... what was the third thing you said?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Homer, you are the worst human being I have ever met.
Can't your old buddy Moe stop by with a list of questions from the Weekly World News? Number one: Sara, is it true you shoplifted a kayak?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I'll have you know she pays full price for all her watercraft!
Aaah, it burns!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: L-Listen, folks, there's no magic formula. I just follow the three C's: clean living, chewing thoroughly, and a daily dose of Vitamin Church.
That guy just don't get it, do he?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: My rumpus room with the new bumper pool table.
Sorry, Homer. I was born a Snake-Handler and I'll die a Snake-Handler.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Neighbor, I heard about your heresy and we've made it our mission to win you back to the flock.
Not before me, you ain't.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Now, now, there's plenty of exits for everyone.
Yeah, we ran out of floorboards there, so we painted the dirt. Pretty clever.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, something is definitely wrong with this hallway!

Yeah, that's enough there, 'Pu. Look, Ned, I know we ain't hung out much, what with your insane fear of drinking and me being banned from the church and all, but ah... but that Maude, she was really something.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Oh, wasn't she? Thank you, Moe. I appreciate that.
Oh, hey, get outta the way, pal. You're blocking the exit.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Ohhh, you want me to stamp your hand so you can get back in?
Oil! Oil!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Only ten dollars to paint my curb like a common whore? Well I'm happy to pay for a three-digit spray! Tell you what, I'll give you another hundred if you paint my garage!
Science! What's science ever done for us? TV off.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Science is like a blabbermouth who ruins a movie by telling you how it ends. Well, I say there are some things we don't want to know! Important things!
Or the Christ Punchers.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: The Chri... I-I-I don't think you understand my objection...
Aw, them stinkin' liars.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: There goes Christmas dinner.
Hey, hey, you can't throw us out. I just made a Cornish game hen with chestnut stuffing. Would you believe a pigeon stuffed with Spam? Would you believe a rat filled with cough drops?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: They've broken every commandment except one!
Eh, sure.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Three... two... one... it's Ash Wednesday everybody! Set down your gins and confess your sins!
Come with me.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Uh, is that your collar, Reverend?
Hey, I don't want no people in here with their evils of alcohol rap.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Wait a second. You're the man at the hospital who reads to sick children.
We haven't got sheltereenees. We want in yours.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well sorry, the shelter's kinda full.
Yeah, that broad is some dame!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You all know Edna?
Aw geez, we been following him for hours.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: You know, with all the energy we're puttin' into this sabotage thing, we coulda written sonnets for our wives, or learned to tango, or lovingly restored one of those antique...
So children, put down your answer sheet and drop that number two!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: As the worm said to the plate of spaghetti, "I... I...
Fire can be our servant, whether it's toasting s'mores, or raining down on Charlie. But it can turn not-so-nice, as you'll see in this skit by the Volunteer Fire Department Players.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Ho-ho! What a great pot party.
As for the school, we are exploring various options to raise the two hundred thousand dollars we need.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: I've got a motorhome I never use. Maybe we should raffle it off.
I'll take it.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Now, folks, nothin' spells fun like rhinestones on a dungaree jacket!
They still have to sign their names properly so we're not totally out of the woods.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Pause the assembly! I have to talk to my wife!
Mother!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Sara, I hate to say it, but your top's upstaging the Pops!
You can't impound my spirit!

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Top of the mornin', Tow-mer!
I will hang up when he leaves.

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, Diane, I've sure enjoyed chatting with you about your problems with your mother.
But how can you afford all this on a widower's salary?

dialogue.speaker: Ned Flanders
dialogue.text: Well, actually, I picked up some extra cash renting out my house to a fraternity.
